risk_taxonomy.area: PNR data consistency across GDS/PSS/check-in touchpoints
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: A PNR desync can mean a passenger is confirmed in one system and wait-listed in another — a boarding-denial risk

risk_taxonomy.area: Fare calculation & rule engine correctness under fare-rule combinatorics
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: Fare rules combine dozens of independent conditions (route, class, season, restrictions); a rule-interaction bug causes revenue leakage or incorrect passenger charges

risk_taxonomy.area: IROPS rebooking logic during mass disruption (weather, ATC ground stop)
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: Rebooking-engine defects during a disruption event affect thousands of passengers simultaneously in a high-visibility, high-emotion context

risk_taxonomy.area: Crew Flight Time Limitation (FTL) compliance calculation
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: An FTL calculation defect is a flight-safety and regulatory-compliance risk, not just a scheduling inconvenience
A missed or misrecorded AD (Airworthiness Directive) compliance item is a direct aviation-safety and regulatory risk
Bag-passenger mismatch is both a security requirement (in many jurisdictions, mandatory) and an operational delay risk

risk_taxonomy.area: Cargo weight & balance calculation integration with load planning
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: Weight-and-balance errors are a direct flight-safety risk, among the highest-consequence defect classes in this domain

risk_taxonomy.area: Interline/codeshare data exchange correctness (baggage, fare, PNR)
risk_taxonomy.why_it_matters: Codeshare/interline defects are hard to reproduce because they only manifest at the boundary between two airlines' systems

compliance_checklist.standard: IATA NDC (New Distribution Capability) / ONE Order
compliance_checklist.note: Increasingly the standard for airline distribution — verify which version/level the AUT targets

compliance_checklist.standard: IATA PADIS / Type B messaging (for legacy PSS integration)
compliance_checklist.applies_to: PNR and departure-control message exchange with GDS/interline partners

compliance_checklist.note: Jurisdiction-specific (EASA FTL vs. FAA Part 117 differ materially)

oracle_library.name: PNR lifecycle state machine
oracle_library.description: created → ticketed → checked-in → boarded → flown/rebooked/cancelled, cross-checked for consistency across GDS, PSS, and DCS (departure control system) at every transition.

oracle_library.name: Fare rule decision table
oracle_library.description: Route x cabin x fare-class x booking-window x change/cancel-rule combinations — fare engines are a textbook decision-table domain given the combinatorial rule structure.

oracle_library.name: IROPS rebooking priority matrix
oracle_library.description: Passenger tier x connection risk x rebooking-inventory availability — determines rebooking sequencing during mass disruption.

oracle_library.name: FTL compliance boundary set
oracle_library.description: Duty-period and rest-period boundaries per the applicable regulatory regime (EASA FTL / FAA Part 117), tested at the exact regulatory limits, not just nominal schedules.

oracle_library.name: Bag-passenger reconciliation matrix
oracle_library.description: Boarded-passenger list x loaded-bag list x offload-triggers (no-show, security hold) — verifies the reconciliation engine correctly triggers bag offload.

data_patterns.format_note: Fake passenger/booking data in valid PNR format, using test-environment record locators that can never collide with a live PNR
Generated fare-rule combinations for rule-engine testing, decoupled from any live published fare
Fake crew schedules at controlled FTL boundary conditions for compliance-engine testing
Fake aircraft tail numbers and maintenance-event data, entirely decoupled from any real fleet

kpi_benchmarks.metric: Fare-quote accuracy vs. filed fare rules

kpi_benchmarks.typical_target: Automated rebooking proposed within minutes of disruption trigger
100% — no tolerance for calculation error given the safety implication

environment_matrix: Crew scheduling sandbox with FTL rule-engine test harness
severity_notes: Weight-and-balance, FTL compliance, and airworthiness-directive tracking defects are treated as flight-safety severity — a category above standard blocker/critical, requiring immediate cross-functional (engineering + safety/compliance) escalation regardless of how the defect was technically introduced.

PNR desync defects during IROPS windows are elevated priority over the same defect class in normal operations, because the blast radius during mass disruption is compressed into a much shorter, higher-stakes window.
Fare-engine defects causing under-charging are commercially severe even though they're 'in the customer's favor' — revenue leakage at scale is a material business risk, not a victimless bug.
